mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances with positive housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the supply contraction signal.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the strong demand signal.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it indicates a robust labor market, which is a strong signal for positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances despite the robust labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the recession signal.
